newsitem.title: USA: NY/NJ Port Authority seen cutting jobs next year.
newsitem.headline: NY/NJ Port Authority seen cutting jobs next year.

text.p: A commissioner to the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, who was appointed by Gov. George Pataki to help make the agency more efficient, predicted that it would cut from 750 to 1,000 jobs next year.

A spokesman for Charles Gargano, who also is chairman of the Empire State Development Corp, quoted him as saying earlier this week that he believed from 750 to 1,000 jobs would have to be eliminated in the next year or so.

"He was speaking in his capacity as vice chairman (of the Port Authority) and that was what he was foreseeing," Gargano's spokesman said. The job reductions predicted by Gargano, which first were reported in the Daily News, would target employees in engineering and legal.

At a commissioners meeting on Thursday, some of the Port Authority's labor relations were harshly criticized by representatives of local unions, while two members of the New York State Assembly urged the agency to reform its practices.
Daniel Feldman, D-Brooklyn, said that he saw a troubling pattern, which seemed to include the threat or declared intention of firing employees.

"This certainly seems to me to be inconsistent with the standards and the way in which we in New York at least, and New Jersey as well, are accustomed to treating labor and the people who work and are employed to carry out the functions of our government and our public authorities," he said.
Similarly, Cartherine Nolan, D-Queens, who chairs the Assembly's standing Committee on Labor, urged the agency to resolve outstanding labor pacts.

"I have been informed that there are numerous instances where labor agreements have been left expired for years at a time," she said in a letter, which was released by Local 1032 of the Communications Workers of America.

One union official, who represents three crafts unions at the P.A.T.H. with around 160 members, said that the union had not had a contract for about two years, while the last negotiating session was almost a year ago.
"Time is running out and I believe a strike is imminent," he said, adding that his local had authorized the leadership to call a strike.
The union official also urged the Port Authority's petition to remove the P.A.T.H. from the oversight of the Federal Railroad Administration be rejected.
